R0147.title: Payment Institution Regulatory Compliance Risk
R0147.definition: Compliance risks faced by payment institutions due to regulatory data quality issues and failure to meet penetrating supervision requirements.
R0147.description: As regulators implement penetrating supervision and payment business supervision for payment institutions, institutions need to provide high-quality regulatory data and keep payment operations, outsourcing, data processing, and risk-control chains traceable. Data quality issues, inconsistent reporting rules, improper data desensitization, weak supplier security management, and inconsistent regulatory reporting scopes may all lead to compliance risk and regulatory penalties.
R0147.influence: May lead to regulatory penalties, business remediation, license risk, reduced partner trust, and increased data-governance and compliance-operation costs.

references.title: Regulation on the Supervision and Administration of Non-bank Payment Institutions

observables: The failure rate of regulatory reporting data validation rises, with key fields missing or inconsistent with regulatory requirements
Reporting data for reserve funds and anti-money laundering shows improper desensitization or recoverable plaintext sensitive information
Security management ledgers for outsourcing partners and suppliers are missing, with access permissions and data processing chains not traceable
The same reporting scope is frequently changed across multiple submissions, failing data consistency checks
